newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Foreign banks plan syndicate to fund Uzbek gold JV.
newsitem.headline: Foreign banks plan syndicate to fund Uzbek gold JV.

text.p: A group of 14 foreign banks plan to set up a syndicate to provide financing for a gold joint venture in the Central Asian state of Uzbekistan, an Uzbek official source said.

Representatives of the banks, including France's Ste Generale and Germany's Dresdner Bank, were due to arrive in Tashkent on Wednesday to discuss the plan, the source in the State Geology and Mineral Resources Committee told Reuters.
The Amantaitau Goldfields venture requires about $350 million in project financing, but it was not clear how much of this would be provided by the banks.

The venture to develop the Amantaitau field is 57 percent owned by Uzbekistan, with a further 35 percent belonging to British conglomerate Lonrho Plc and eight percent to the International Finance Corp, a unit of the World Bank.
Lonrho won a tender earlier this year to take part in the project in the Central Asian state's Navoi province.

The Uzbek newspaper Business Partner said it involved the development of four open quarries, one underground mine and construction of an ore enrichment facility, which should come on stream in the first quarter of 1998.
Uzbek official sources and representatives of Lonrho in Tashkent declined to estimate reserves.
Business Partner said the project's life could be 12-17 years.
Trade journals say Uzbekistan is the world's ninth largest gold producer, with output last year of 63.6 tonnes.
President Islam Karimov has said the desert nation has gold reserves of around 5,000 tonnes. --Tashkent newsroom +3712 361958
